title: 4 things you didn't know you could do with Gemini
content_html:
Published Sep 30, 2026, 8:00 AM EDT

Parth is a technology analyst and writer specializing in the comprehensive review and feature exploration of the Android ecosystem. His work focus on productivity apps and flagship devices, particularly Google Pixel and Samsung mobile hardware and software.

He provides expert guidance on productivity software, system optimization, and the advanced functionalities that allow users to maximize their device's potential. His analyses are crucial resources for readers seeking to master complex operating system features and streamline their digital workflows.

When he is not busy with technical analysis and software evaluation, Parth dedicates his time to watching K-dramas, studying mobile technology trends and the role of artificial intelligence.

I use Gemini almost every day, but for a long time, I treated it like a smarter version of Google Search.

I would ask questions, summarize text, rewrite a paragraph, and move on.

After I started digging through its integrations and lesser-known features, I realized I was barely using what it could actually do.

Some of these features are easy to miss, while others only become useful once you know the right way to use them.

Create schedules in Gemini

Automate your workflow like a pro

One of my favorite Gemini features is Scheduled inside the Spark menu.

This goes beyond asking Gemini to remind me about something at a certain time.

I use it to cut down on repetitive checking during my workday. For example, I can ask Gemini to scan my Gmail, Calendar, and Drive every morning and give me a quick rundown of deadlines, important emails, and documents I may need to revisit.

During the NFL season, I can create a schedule to give me all the details about last week's major updates on a Monday morning.

For my tech writing workflow, another useful setup is monitoring topics like Android, AI, local LLMs, Docker, or updates on Google apps.

Schedules work with Gemini's connected apps and skills, so I am not limited to receiving a generic reminder.

Gemini can gather information, organize it, and perform supported actions as part of the workflow.

Check out my dedicated post to learn more about Gemini Schedules.

Using Gemini as the control center for my mobile apps

Use @ to call specific services

After I connect services such as Google Workspace, WhatsApp, Canva, Messages, YouTube Music, Google Photos, and more to Gemini, it becomes a single place to pull information and take action.

For example, I can ask Gemini to pull my top three pictures from the Hanoi trip or the top shots from my son's recent birthday party, and it does the job in no time.

I don't need to open Google Photos and search for pictures.

That's only half the story. I can combine multiple steps into one natural-language request.

For example, if I am planning a Japan trip, I can ask Gemini to find my hotel confirmation from Gmail, add the check-in time to Google Calendar, and create a packing checklist in Google Tasks.

That saves me from opening Gmail, copying the details, switching to Calendar, creating an event, and then opening Tasks separately.

Gemini is usually good at figuring out which connected app I mean.

But if I want it to look for information in a specific app, I use @ and mention a service in the search box.

This is helpful when the same type of information exists in several places.

Instead of saying, "Find my article notes about Android Auto," I can type @Google Keep and tell Gemini to look there.

Turn deep research into something else

Explore Gemini Notebooks

Gemini Notebooks takes the entire research experience to the next level.

I can add PDFs, websites, YouTube videos, Docs, Slides, and other sources to a notebook, then use the same research material to generate different outputs.

Depending on what I need, I can create an Audio Overview, Video Overview, slide deck, infographic, flashcards, quiz, and more from these sources.

Suppose I am researching a complicated self-hosting tool and have collected Google documentation, support pages, YouTube demonstrations, and a few PDFs.

I can keep those sources in one notebook, ask questions about them, and generate an Audio Overview to understand the topic quickly.

Students will love this feature for study purposes.

Use Gemini Live in supported apps

It's a game-changer

The recently announced Gemini Live has been a game-changer for my productivity.

I find Keep Live useful because ideas rarely arrive in a neat format.

If an article idea pops into my head, I can basically brain-dump it:

Create a note for my Samsung battery article. Add sections for overnight drain, Modes and Routines, power saving, and before-and-after results.

Gemini can organize that rambling into a structured note.

I can even ask it to add the info to an existing note, and it does the job in no time. The same concept extends to Docs and Gmail.

The possibilities are endless here. You can check my dedicated post to learn everything about Gemini Live in Google Keep.

Unlock more from Google's AI

The more I use Gemini, the more I realize that the obvious features are only the starting point.

The real value comes from combining things like schedules, app integrations, notebooks, and Gemini Live in my routine.

That is where I would encourage you to experiment.

You don't need to use every feature here. Pick the ones that solve a real problem, and get creative with them.

When you start approaching Gemini this way, it feels like a flexible productivity layer across your devices and apps.
